items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: And we worked together for one solid year without taking any jobs, any engagements. See, then she started to and took an engagement, and I was more like a manager than an accompanist, you see.

ctx.x: And a lot of musicians of your generation could not see bop music, you know. How did you feel about it?

I wasn't even interested in it. I'll tell you why, because as I told you, I didn't have any need to hear any band because I was through with black bands. You see, because the musicians after that Pleasure Beach Park episode, I

said, 'Well, look. I don't want any ulcers. So the best thing I can do is stay away from bands.' So I used to talk French. We'd go sometimes to Montreal and visit and talk some French, you know. And come on back here. And I had a studio. Had a studio over here on LaSalle Street. It was LaSalle Street then. Now LaSalle Street has gone into an apartment house over there. Well, I had a studio over here. And I taught -- that was how Rae Ray's mother brought her to me, was in this studio, you see. And we worked…
